_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) at risk of rapid disease progression, generally a UPCR >= 1.5 g/g; approved under accelerated approval based on reduction of proteinuria.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to atrasentan or placebo (133 centers, 20 countries).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with biopsy-proven primary IgAN on maximally tolerated RASi, eGFR >= 30 mL/min/1.73 m^2, and UPCR >= 1 g/g; a subset on SGLT2i were in an exploratory stratum not in the primary analysis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in proteinuria (UPCR based on 24-hour urine collection) from baseline to Week 36 in the main stratum.
pivotal_trials.n: 404 randomized (main stratum 340: atrasentan 170, placebo 170; SGLT2i stratum 64); 403 received at least one dose (201 atrasentan, 202 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: Trial met its primary endpoint; at Week 36, UPCR was reduced 36% versus placebo (95% CI: 26%, 45%; one-sided p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) were peripheral edema (10% atrasentan vs 8% placebo) and anemia (7% vs 2%); also hypotension (6% vs 4%) and ALT/AST >3x ULN (2% vs 1%). Hemoglobin decrease >2 g/dL was 20% vs 5%. Serious AEs in 6% (atrasentan) vs 5% (placebo). Class risks include hepatotoxicity, fluid retention, decreased sperm counts.
target_moa: Atrasentan is a selective endothelin type A receptor (ETA R) antagonist (>1800-fold selectivity over ETB); endothelin-1 contributes to IgAN pathogenesis, and by antagonizing ETA R atrasentan reduces proteinuria.
modality: Small molecule (oral endothelin receptor antagonist, 0.75-mg tablet once daily).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — VANRAFIA is contraindicated in pregnant patients; it may cause major birth defects based on animal data. Exclude pregnancy before initiation and advise effective contraception.

rems.type: No REMS required; the review team concluded labeling (Boxed Warning and contraception measures) is adequate to mitigate the embryo-fetal toxicity risk, and the REMS Oversight Committee agreed a REMS is not necessary.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held because the application did not raise significant or controversial issues meriting outside expertise, and due to concerns that public release of information could impact the integrity of the ongoing trial.

surrogate_endpoint.text: A substantial reduction in proteinuria (UPCR at Week 36) accepted as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for disease progression (loss of kidney function) in IgAN.

citations.quote: Based on the available data, the Division of Cardiology and Nephrology (the Division) accepts a substantial reduction in proteinuria as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for disease progression (loss of kidney function) in IgAN and as a basis for accelerated approval (Thompson et al. 2019).

The Applicant submitted the results of a prespecified interim analysis on the treatment effect on UPCR at Week 36 compared to baseline from an adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trial (ALIGN trial) in subjects with primary, biopsy-proven IgAN and proteinuria.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Required (PMR 4829-1) to conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to describe and verify the clinical benefit of atrasentan for primary IgA nephropathy; the ongoing ALIGN trial's final analysis will verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: 4829-1 Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to describe and verify the clinical benefit of atrasentan for the treatment of primary IgA nephropathy. The trial should be adequately powered and of sufficient
As noted above, the ALIGN trial is ongoing, and the primary endpoint at the final analysis in this trial will be used to verify and describe the clinical benefit.

summary.text: Standard review NDA granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR Part 314, Subpart H, based on reduction of proteinuria (UPCR at Week 36) as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint, with the ongoing ALIGN trial required as the confirmatory trial to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: The Applicant is seeking approval under the provisions of 21 CFR Part 314, Subpart H, utilizing proteinuria as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint. The Applicant has an ongoing trial, ALIGN, that is intended to confirm the clinical benefit in the postmarketing setting.

The Applicant submitted the results of a prespecified interim analysis on the treatment effect on UPCR at Week 36 compared to baseline from an adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trial (ALIGN trial) in subjects with primary, biopsy-proven IgAN and proteinuria.
